title: Bookkeeping and Accounting for Small Businesses

questions.q: In "Accounts and the equation Define", which of these is a key idea?
o: List all balances in a trial balance with debit and credit columns.
Calculate tax collected on sales less tax paid on purchases to find the payable amount.
Group accounts into assets, liabilities, equity, income and expense.
Record bank charges and interest found only in the statement.

questions.q: In "Record source documents Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Match each bank line to the cash book entry.
Number and file documents in date order, paper or scanned.
List all balances in a trial balance with debit and credit columns.
Post each entry to its ledger account and find the balance of each account.

questions.q: In "Journal entries Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Record a cash sale: debit cash, credit sales.
List all balances in a trial balance with debit and credit columns.
Check that assets equal liabilities plus equity including profit.
Debit increases assets and expenses; credit increases liabilities, equity and income.

questions.q: In "Ledger and trial balance Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Divide the difference by nine to see if two digits were swapped.
Produce the trial balance and statements.
Collect invoices, bills, receipts, bank entries and cash vouchers for every transaction.
Record the payment of expenses such as rent and wages with evidence.

questions.q: In "Bank and cash reconciliation Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Record bank charges and interest found only in the statement.
Build a chart of accounts with codes, for example 1000 for assets and 4000 for income.
Number and file documents in date order, paper or scanned.
Present findings, errors found and fixes to a mentor.

questions.q: In "Profit and loss and balance sheet Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Check that assets equal liabilities plus equity including profit.
Post each entry to its ledger account and find the balance of each account.
Count physical cash and compare with the book balance.
If the totals differ, check the difference for a missing posting or a flipped entry.

questions.q: In "Tax, payroll and controls Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Calculate tax collected on sales less tax paid on purchases to find the payable amount.
Record the payment of expenses such as rent and wages with evidence.
List all balances in a trial balance with debit and credit columns.

questions.q: In "Capstone: a month of books Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set controls: two people for cash, approvals for payments, monthly reconciliation.
Check each bill for date, name, amount, tax number and tax amount.
Record bank charges and interest found only in the statement.
Produce the trial balance and statements.
